title: String band and Jack Laine's bands
summary: He joined Gus Miller's string band, then played for Jack Laine, whom he credits as the father of the white bands, and who fed musicians.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Okay, to answer that, then, do you want to stop? Okay, let's see, you were talking about when you first started on your carnet. Yeah. You told about that Italian wedding. Mm-hmm. And you heard other tunes.
Yeah, and then we... Well, little by little, we got into Miller, Gus Miller and I got into a little string band deal, you know?
Violin, guitar, bass, cornton, clannin'. And we plugged around a little around, first thing you know, we run into... Oh, we're done... I started playing with Jack Lane. Oh, yeah. I know him.
Oh, Jack. He's still well. He is, huh? He's talked about you. We interviewed him.
He's a grand old guy. He still looks well. He is, Jack. Well, I'm glad. No, no, a lot of people didn't give Jack credit. But Jack started, they were one of those guys out.
That's right, I think so too, from when I trained. You betcha.

And I'm the guy I can tell you, because I was one of the guys who started. And everybody around there worked for Jack. Jack made that, it was his life. He had maybe four or five bands going, see? And everybody who wanted a job would see Jack. You get this, no matter who you were away, he could use you. But he was a smart guy with us. Go to his wife, go to his house. What'd you have? Big pot of soup, plate of stew, coffee, anything you want. Always have something on the stove. And many of the day, boy, it felt pretty good.
So, but really, like I said, they didn't give Jack a lot of these books that they write around in. Nobody touches Jack. And he was really the daddy.
You used to start off with the original Dixieland jazz band, something like that. Yeah, yeah. And they used to get all about the other fellas that came before them.

Well, courses like everything else, they bypass a lot of stuff. The real things, you know. That's right. A lot of people do that. But I don't know. He, uh, then we, uh, played with Bill Gallaty's band.
